usage:
faildrill breaks a Tyk install on purpose and measures what callers saw.

Usage:
  faildrill preflight [flags]            read the install, change nothing
  faildrill run <drill> [flags]          run one drill while traffic flows
  faildrill export record.json...        bundle records for the replay page
  faildrill version

Drills:
  redis-primary     take the Redis primary away        --fault crash | hang
  gateway-pod       take one gateway pod away          --fault crash | evict
  rolling-restart   restart every gateway pod, as an upgrade does

Run "faildrill preflight -h" or "faildrill run -h" for the flags.
preflight:
gateway    gateway-tyk-tyk-gateway  (docker.tyk.io/tyk-gateway/tyk-gateway:v5.13.5)
namespace  faildrill-lab

ok    2 gateway replicas
WARN  all 2 gateway pods run on one node (outage-arena01)
      Losing that node takes every gateway with it. Replicas only help when they are apart.
      see it happen: faildrill run gateway-pod
WARN  no PodDisruptionBudget covers the gateway
      A node drain or cluster upgrade may evict every gateway pod at the same time.
      see it happen: faildrill run gateway-pod
WARN  the gateway has no preStop hook
      A stopping pod gets SIGTERM while the Service is still sending it requests; removing it from the endpoints takes a few seconds to reach every node.
      see it happen: faildrill run rolling-restart
note  readiness probe /hello every 10s, unready after 3 failures (30s)
      A pod that stops being able to serve keeps receiving traffic for that long before Kubernetes takes it out.
WARN  rolling update allows 1 unavailable of 2
      During every upgrade the gateway runs below strength; with few replicas that is a large share of capacity.
      see it happen: faildrill run rolling-restart
ok    the gateway finds Redis through Sentinel (master name "mymaster", redis-sentinel:26379)
ok    3 Redis pods
ok    every Redis pod has a persistent volume

4 warnings. Preflight reads the install; only a drill shows what callers would feel.
